items.areaDesc: San Diego County Coastal Areas; San Bernardino and Riverside County Valleys-The Inland Empire; San Diego County Inland Valleys; Santa Ana Mountains and Foothills; Orange County Coastal; Orange County Inland
items.classification: FACT about the issued alert; hazard is conditional
items.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions with high temperatures on the
hottest days ranging from around 90 near the coast to the upper 90s
to 108 for the valleys possible. Low temperatures for coastal areas
into the western valleys will warm into the lower to mid 70s during
the weekend with those warm overnight temperatures continuing for
next week.

* WHERE...Orange County Coastal Areas, Orange County Inland Areas,
San Bernardino and Riverside County Valleys-The Inland Empire, San
Diego County Coastal Areas, San Diego County Valleys, and Santa Ana
Mountains and Foothills.

* WHEN...From Friday morning through Wednesday evening.

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat events.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A long-duration heat wave is expected to
develop late this week and continue through much of next week into
the following weekend with Moderate or greater HeatRisk for the
coast and valleys and Major to Extreme HeatRisk for inland coastal
areas into the western valleys.

items.areaDesc: San Diego County Coastal Areas; Orange County Coastal
items.classification: FACT about the issued alert; hazard is conditional
items.description:
* WHAT...Minor coastal flooding expected due to high tides and
high baseline water levels.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...Until 5 PM PDT today.

* IMPACTS...Minor coastal flooding and minor coastal erosion
expected during high tides, most likely between 11 AM and 1 PM.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides are expected to peak between
6.9 and 7.1 feet between 11 AM and 1 PM today. These tide
predictions have been corrected to reflect current trends in
observed tide observations.

items.areaDesc: San Francisco; North Bay Interior Valleys; San Francisco Bay Shoreline; Northern Monterey Bay; Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast
items.classification: FACT about the issued alert; hazard is conditional
items.description:
* WHAT...Up to 1.2 ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Bayshore locations along the San Francisco Bay, San
Pablo Bay, and Monterey Bay.

* WHEN...Now through 5 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. High tides will result in
flooding along coastal trails, cut off access to some low-
lying beaches and coastal areas, and bring water and waves
farther up the beach than typical.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.2 ft above normal (7.03 ft MLLW) at 2:10 PM
Wednesday 9/30, and 1.1 ft above normal (6.92 ft MLLW) at 2:58
PM Thursday 10/01. These predictions include up to 0.7 ft of
surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding
threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along
the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay,
respectively.

items.areaDesc: Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands; Ventura County Beaches; Malibu Coast; Los Angeles County Beaches
items.classification: FACT about the issued alert; hazard is conditional
items.description:
* WHAT...Strong rip currents. Minor tidal overflows, especially
during the late morning high tides.

* WHERE...Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands, Ventura County
Beaches, Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches.

* WHEN...Through Wednesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Pooling of sea water is possible around high tide at
beach and harbor areas that is uncommon with normal tidal
ranges. Enhanced beach erosion is also possible. No significant
damage is expected. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers
out to sea.
